system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)
Context: EXERCISE / DRILL
Target area (chosen by the operator): Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-02-16, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/byrq247-national-centre-meteorology-warns-dust-reduced] ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Met office reviewer objects (headline): The alert confines the hazard to Abu Dhabi, but the NCM bulletin names no emirate; 'ABU DHABI' is only the WAM dateline. The headline also drops 'some', which makes the hazard sound as if it covers all coastal and inland Abu Dhabi. Fix: Describe the area as the bulletin does. For example, in the headline: 'EXERCISE: Blowing dust reducing visibility in some coastal and inland areas until 18:00'. In the description: 'in some coastal and inland areas (per NCM)'. Remove 'Abu Dhabi' unless NCM confirms that area. | Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): No protective action in either language. The phone text gives the hazard, valid-until time and source but no instruction to recipients, so the first page does not carry the action. Fix: Add a short protective action in both English and Arabic, placed right after the hazard so it falls on the first page or as early as possible. For example: 'Drive with caution, keep a safe distance and use low-beam lights; people with respiratory conditions should stay indoors.' Keep the Arabic within the 15-page limit (UCS-2, 41 characters a page). [cites Common Alerting Protocol Version 1.2, 3.2.2 "info" Element and Sub-elements]

data.headline: EXERCISE: Blowing dust reducing visibility in some coastal and inland areas until 18:00
data.description: EXERCISE. Strong NW winds are blowing dust and sand, cutting visibility below 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas (per NCM). Drive with caution on open roads. Until 18:00 today, 16 Feb. Info: alerts.example.ae
data.instruction: Drive with caution, especially on external and open roads. Be ready for sudden drops in visibility from blowing dust.
left_out: 'Abu Dhabi' as the hazard area: the NCM bulletin names no emirate. 'ABU DHABI' is only the WAM dateline, so the area is given as the bulletin states it.

Suggested advice to 'keep a safe distance', 'use low-beam lights' and 'people with respiratory conditions should stay indoors': this advice is not in the NCM bulletin. The instruction keeps to NCM's own advice: exercise caution, especially when driving on external and open roads.
Arabic phone text: this draft covers the English fields only. The Arabic version, within the 15-page UCS-2 limit, must be prepared separately.
data.note_for_reviewer: The operator's target zone is labelled Abu Dhabi, but the text now uses NCM's wording 'some coastal and inland areas', as the Met reviewer asked. Please confirm the broadcast polygon still fits, and decide whether NCM should approve the extra driving and health advice before it is added.
